A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same consistency-based segmentation-ranking work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material are readable and can be matched despite extensive rewriting, renaming, and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-ranking experiments for semantic and instance segmentation, including post-UDA evaluation, perturbation sweeps, and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, revised ToothFairy2 results, and an illustrated post-UDA failure case.

M1.justification: CTE is renamed CMR, retaining the perturb-and-compare procedure, EI/NHD/ARS scores, input/feature perturbations, and median aggregation. However, v2 specifies a weighted average across semantic classes, whereas v3 specifies an average without clarifying the weights. Whether this represents a small aggregation change or merely revised wording is unresolved.

E1.justification: The mitochondria, nuclei, cell, Covid-IF, and ToothFairy2 datasets and the classification, semantic/instance segmentation, direct-transfer, post-UDA, and supervised fine-tuning scenarios are retained. Adding TotalSegmentator changes the candidate model set, not the represented dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Nuclear Norm (NuNo) and Dispersion to the microscopy comparisons, TS/NuNo/Dispersion to ToothFairy2 Table 2, and SEG to the previously baseline-free instance comparison in Table 4. Conversely, TS disappears from the supervised fine-tuning comparison, v2 Table 25 versus v3 Table 17. Hscore remains in the appendix despite its omission from the main summary table.

E3.justification: The reported ToothFairy2 model bank increases from seven to eight with TotalSegmentator. New comparisons specify correlating overall 3D baseline rankings with per-group performance and evaluating SEG with agreement ratio 0.75 and an estimated centroid radius. Existing data splits, training hardware/budgets, and correlation measures are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.5 and Figure 5 add visual and numerical evidence for the previously discussed EPFL-to-VNC Mean Teacher failure. The ToothFairy2 EI sensitivity results are revised, while most perturbation sweeps and the Covid-IF failure examples are retained. SEG sensitivity is discussed, but no separate parameter sweep is supplied in the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across target datasets and correlation p-values with the same significance thresholds. Additional baseline rows follow these practices. No new repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Substantial new baseline results are reported: Table 4 gives SEG mean Kendall correlations of 0.12 for cells and 0.48 for nuclei, alongside retained Gaussian CMR values of 0.69 and 0.72. ToothFairy2 EI sweep values also change, under the reported expanded model bank, and Figure 2 switches from Hmito to EPFL. TS fine-tuning results are removed. Most retained microscopy and UDA results are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 corrects and expands the ARS joint-overlap and marginal definitions and adds a split/merge harmonic-mean decomposition in Equation 4. However, its denominators omit the squared marginals required to recover Equation 3. This is a limited mathematical revision; no substantial theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim of effective unsupervised, source-free segmentation-model ranking is retained. Novelty is qualified by acknowledging SEG, replacing the earlier assertion that no instance-ranking baseline exists with an emphasis on a unified, pixel-level, black-box-compatible framework for heterogeneous repositories.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for similar hard/soft consistency performance, SEG's centroid and shape limitations, and the method's memory advantage in 3D. It also clarifies the limited post-UDA VNC test sample and qualifies generalist-model failures. Existing task-alignment, collapsed-output, and boundary-sensitive-metric limitations remain substantially intact.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies perturbation-strength sampling, mAP@[0.5:0.95] for retained instance results, SEG parameters, Mean Teacher updates without pseudo-label selection, and the two-slice post-UDA VNC test set. These mainly expand documentation rather than establish changed experiments. The earlier promise to release code upon acceptance is removed without a replacement project-access link.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands into performance estimation, quality control, ensemble agreement, and segmentation failure detection. New discussion of NuNo, Dispersion, SEG, and ODP-Bench supports explicit distinctions between repository ranking, calibrated uncertainty, single-model quality control, and fine-tuning transferability. This materially revises the work's positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methods, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. CTE becomes CMR, motivation precedes the formal problem definition, model and evaluation descriptions are combined, and the appendix is reorganized into lettered sections with a dedicated UDA explanation.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial figure and table redesign. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 2–4 are revised, Table 1 is split into supervised/unsupervised panels, and many appendix sweeps are merged into subtables. The old failure figures become Figure 6 panels, while a new UDA failure visualization becomes Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The added unsupervised comparisons, especially SEG in Table 4, address an important gap in v2's comparative evidence and improve its novelty positioning. Additional protocol details and the UDA failure visualization improve transparency. These gains are tempered by the new inconsistency between ARS Equations 3 and 4 and the absence of the supplementary SEG sensitivity evidence invoked by the discussion.
